samples.question: Four coloured towers of square blocks stand on one baseline. The black triangle below the baseline is the pointer, and it starts under the tower shown. The square cards along the bottom are operations, applied one at a time in order from left to right, as the long arrow above them shows. A dark slate card carrying white dots adds that many blocks to the tower the pointer is under at that moment. A grey card carrying a white triangle moves the pointer one tower in the direction the triangle points and adds nothing. The pointer never has to leave the four towers, no tower is ever emptied, and the final arrangement is not drawn. The black ring at the top marks one tower, the ringed tower. After every card has been applied, how many blocks does the ringed tower hold? Answer with a number.
